correctness.rationale: For distinct primes \(p<q\), \(\sigma(pq)=(p+1)(q+1)\). Cross-divisibility shows \(pq\) is Duffinian exactly when \(p\ne2\) and \(q\not\equiv-1\pmod p\). For exceptional odd \(p\le x^{1/3}\), Brun–Titchmarsh gives \(\pi(x/p;p,-1)\ll x/[p(p-1)\log x]\), summable over \(p\). For \(x^{1/3}<p<\sqrt{x}\), discarding the congruence and using \(\pi(x/p)\ll x/[p\log x]\) leaves a bounded reciprocal-prime sum over a fixed logarithmic interval. The \(p=2\) contribution is also \(O(x/\log x)\). Thus the exceptional set is \(O(x/\log x)\), negligible relative to Landau's \(x\log\log x/\log x\) count of squarefree semiprimes. The finite checker confirms only the local criterion, not the asymptotic proof.
risks: No leading constant for the exceptional semiprimes is proved.

originality.rationale: Pollack's full 2011 paper studies the global distribution of \(\gcd(n,\sigma(n))\) and uses the same \(-1\) congruence/Brun–Titchmarsh mechanism, but full-document searches found no occurrence of 'semiprime' or 'Duffinian' and no theorem conditioning on the two-prime stratum. The global density behavior is qualitatively opposite to the audited relative-density-one result. value.rationale: The theorem exposes a genuine density reversal: a globally sparse coprimality property becomes generic on the natural squarefree-semiprime stratum. The exact local criterion and quantitative \(O(x/\log x)\) exceptional bound make this a motivated analytic-number-theory fact rather than a finite sequence observation.
risks: The result is only a relative-density statement for squarefree semiprimes and does not quantify a leading exceptional constant.

limitations: Squarefree products of two distinct primes only.
